query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the spray distance during HVAF-i7 deposition to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity and deposition efficiency, enabling thicker FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats without compromising the oxidation resistance and adhesion quality.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with 15–45 μm particles, known from previous work to yield high-quality coatings with minimal as‐sprayed oxidation on similar systems.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 process by increasing the nozzle-to-substrate distance to around 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition under elevated temperature conditions appropriate for high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including applications with internal diameters as small as 120 mm, while maintaining the required minimal oxidation and adhesion standards.
generation.structural_mediator: The higher particle velocity induced by an increased spray distance promotes stronger inter-particle bonding and higher deposition efficiency.
generation.mechanism: By increasing the spray distance, particles gain higher momentum before impact, similar to observations in prior studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats. This enhanced kinetic energy leads to more effective peening and interlocking upon impact, thereby building up a thicker coating while maintaining the desired chemical stability and microstructural quality.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline where the HVAF-i7 process yields acceptable coating quality but insufficient thickness, it is predicted that this intervention will produce a thicker, adherent bond coat that still exhibits minimal oxidation and maintains performance under high-temperature service.
generation.baseline: Standard HVAF-i7 deposition using 15–45 μm feedstock at the original spray distance, which achieves acceptable coating quality but falls short in coating thickness.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of this intervention is expected under controlled deposition conditions with the specified feedstock and for internal geometries around 120 mm diameter. Deviations in feedstock characteristics or significant changes in substrate geometry may lead to different outcomes.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in deposition efficiency and resultant coating thickness is uncertain and may depend on precise torch settings and environmental conditions during spraying.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled series of depositions using the HVAF-i7 torch on identical substrates. In one set, use the standard spray distance and in the other, use a 300–350 mm spray distance. Evaluate and compare the coating thickness, oxidation levels, and adhesion strength. Post-deposition, subject the coatings to thermal cycling to assess durability.
measurements: Coating thickness (measured by cross-sectional microscopy or profilometry)
Surface oxidation level (via XPS or colorimetric analysis)
Durability after thermal cycling (via thermal barrier performance tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If coatings deposited at 300–350 mm do not show a statistically significant increase in thickness over the baseline or if the increased distance leads to unacceptable levels of oxidation or degradation in adhesion or durability, the hypothesis will be falsified.

citation_validation.initial_error: generated hypothesis cites unavailable evidence: ['HVAF-M3 study: optimal feedstock 15–45 μm', 'MCrAlY bond coats study: slight gain in deposition efficiency at 300–350 mm spray distance']
